task.prompt:
Please create or replace a PostgreSQL PL/pgSQL procedure named `sp(arg1 integer, arg2 text, arg3 text, arg4 integer, arg5 text, arg6 integer)`.

Return the complete stored procedure, and nothing else. It should return no rows and have no output arguments. The attached examples are worked cases to check against.

Parameters by position: `arg1` is the starting threshold, `arg2` is the starting status and restaurant-name pattern, `arg3` is the operation text used for street-location and city-code comparisons, `arg4` is the student-number anchor, `arg5` is the student last name to match, and `arg6` is the restaurant-kind-number anchor.

Only the restaurant, student, restaurant-kind, visit-record, and restaurant-kind-link-record business data mentioned here is in scope. Start with threshold `arg1`, status `arg2`, operation `arg3`, handled-row count 0, batch size 10, state `INIT`, and no high priority seen. Status only changes during restaurant-kind processing; operation never changes; threshold only changes when the student rule adds a student number to it.

Pick the mode from the initial threshold. Below 3, process restaurants numbered below `arg1` whose names match `arg2` with `LIKE`, state `MINIMAL_PROCESS`. Below 8, process students numbered from `arg4 - 5` through `arg4 + 15`, state `STANDARD_PROCESS`. Below 18, process restaurant kinds numbered above `arg6 - 20`, state `ENHANCED_PROCESS`. Below 25, mark restaurants numbered below `arg1` whose name is not the current status with street location `ARCHIVED`, state `ARCHIVE_MODE`, and do no row loop. Below 40, delete students below `arg4` with last name `OBSOLETE`, state `CLEANUP_MODE`, and do no row loop. Otherwise, renumber restaurant kinds above 200 to `arg6 + 100`, state `BOOST_MODE`, and do no row loop.

For row-processing modes, use natural result order and increment the handled-row count before handling each row. In `MINIMAL_PROCESS`, a fetched restaurant number above 25 gets name `PROMOTED`; otherwise, if its street location equals the operation text, delete its visit records, restaurant-kind link records, and then the restaurant matching the fetched number and name; otherwise set that restaurant number’s street location to `PENDING`. In `STANDARD_PROCESS`, first set sex `U` when the fetched city code equals `arg3`, then set city code `MATCHED` when the fetched last name equals `arg5`; after that, last names matching `ACTIVE%` become `PROCESSED`, else fetched student numbers above `arg4 + 5` are added to the threshold, else delete the fetched-number student whose last name is `EXPIRED`. In `ENHANCED_PROCESS`, classify the fetched restaurant-kind number as `LOW_PRIORITY` below 50, `MEDIUM_PRIORITY` below 150, or `HIGH_PRIORITY` otherwise, remembering if high priority was ever seen; then add 10 to restaurant-kind numbers currently equal to that fetched original number. After each handled row, once the handled-row count reaches the current batch size, increase the batch size by 5.

After all mode work, perform only the first applicable final action: if status is `HIGH_PRIORITY` or high priority was ever seen, double restaurant-kind numbers above 100; otherwise if state is `ARCHIVE_MODE`, delete `ARCHIVED` restaurants below `threshold - 10`; otherwise if more than 15 rows were handled, set last name `BULK_PROCESSED` for students numbered from `arg4` through `arg4 + 50`; otherwise set the name of restaurants numbered above the current threshold to the operation text.

Use normal PostgreSQL behavior, and don’t catch errors or manage transactions inside the procedure.

materials.text:
# Calling the procedure

Invoke it with `CALL`, not as a function. The arguments are positional and use the declaration `sp(arg1 integer, arg2 text, arg3 text, arg4 integer, arg5 text, arg6 integer)`; the main request explains what each one means.
